Two sources selected: (1) Leiva-Peña, Rubí-González and Vicente-Parada 2021 'Social Determinants of Mental Health: Public Policies Based on the Biopsychosocial Model in Latin American Countries' (Rev Panam Salud Publica, DOI 10.26633/RPSP.2021.158, PMC8678097, CC-BY-NC-ND 3.0 IGO) — a Spanish/English/Portuguese trilingual open-access review of Latin American mental health policy through the biopsychosocial lens; (2) De Marco 2006 'Do modelo biomédico ao modelo biopsicossocial: um projeto de educação permanente' (Revista Brasileira de Educação Médica, DOI 10.1590/S0100-55022006000100010, CC-BY-NC 4.0, SciELO) — a Portuguese-language Brazilian article on the transition from biomedical to biopsychosocial model in medical education. items.title: The Biopsychosocial Model 40 Years On
items.rights_note: Chapter 1 in: Bolton D, Gillett G (2019). The Biopsychosocial Model of Health and Disease: New Philosophical and Scientific Developments. Palgrave Pivot (DOI 10.1007/978-3-030-11899-0_1). Book is open access via Springer/OAPEN (Creative Commons). Chapter text accessible on NCBI Bookshelf without paywall. Places Engel's 1977 proposal in 40-year historical context with philosophical critique.

items.title: The Need for a New Medical Model: A Challenge for Biomedicine
items.rights_note: Science 196(4286):129-136, 8 April 1977. DOI 10.1126/science.847460. Full text paywalled at science.org (returned 403 this session). Institutional PDF found at URMC Rochester (349KB) but rights status unclear; not cached. Caching NCBI E-utilities official abstract XML as formal bibliographic pointer. This is abstract-level only, not full-text evidence.

items.title: The Clinical Application of the Biopsychosocial Model
items.rights_note: American Journal of Psychiatry 137(5):535-544, May 1980. DOI 10.1176/ajp.137.5.535. Full text paywalled at AJP online. PACES Connection hosts a 1.6MB scan PDF but rights status unclear; not cached. Caching NCBI E-utilities official abstract XML as formal bibliographic pointer. This is abstract-level only, not full-text evidence.

items.title: The Biopsychosocial Model 25 Years Later: Principles, Practice, and Scientific Inquiry
items.rights_note: Annals of Family Medicine 2(6):576-582, November 2004. DOI 10.1370/afm.245. PMC open-access subset; no explicit CC license stated (copyright Annals of Family Medicine Inc.). The most-cited methodological synthesis of the biopsychosocial model: defines the model as both philosophy of clinical care and practical guide; discusses three core properties (multileveled, patient-centred, relational); not to be conflated with WHO-ICF or generic holistic care slogans.

items.title: The biopsychosocial model: not dead, but in need of revival
items.rights_note: BJPsych Bulletin 46(4):232-234, 2022. DOI 10.1192/bjb.2022.29. Creative Commons Attribution (CC-BY 4.0). Independent commentary examining the model's validity (does it accurately describe causes of illness?), usefulness (does it help clinicians?), and implementation (why is it poorly applied in practice?). Distinct from the Bolton 2023 empirical/theoretical revision in empirical_status.

items.title: A Revitalized Biopsychosocial Model: Core Theory, Research Paradigms, and Clinical Implications
items.rights_note: Psychological Medicine 53(16), 2023. DOI 10.1017/S0033291723002660. Creative Commons Attribution (CC-BY 4.0). Provides the most recent systematic theoretical and empirical evaluation of the model's scientific content. Argues the model has scientific content through condition-specific causal models, not through vacuous general statements. Distinct from Williamson 2022 critique; this source proposes a revitalized version with testable research paradigms.

items.title: Biopsychosocial Model in Contemporary Psychiatry: Current Validity and Future Prospects
items.rights_note: Indian Journal of Psychological Medicine 41(6), 2019. DOI 10.4103/IJPSYM.IJPSYM_314_19. Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 (CC-BY-NC-SA). Reviews the current use of the biopsychosocial model in psychiatric training and practice, its limitations and future directions. Non-Western (Indian) psychiatric perspective; does not conflate biopsychosocial model with WHO-ICF or with integrative medicine more broadly.

items.title: Social Determinants of Mental Health: Public Policies Based on the Biopsychosocial Model in Latin American Countries
items.rights_note: Revista Panamericana de Salud Publica (PAHO), December 2021. DOI 10.26633/RPSP.2021.158. Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivs 3.0 IGO (CC-BY-NC-ND 3.0 IGO). Published in English, Spanish and Portuguese. Examines advances and challenges in implementing biopsychosocial model-based mental health policies in Latin America through Web of Science, Scopus, PubMed and SciELO sources. Latin American applications and policy contexts are distinct from Engel's original medical model and from WHO-ICF.

items.title: Do modelo biomédico ao modelo biopsicossocial: um projeto de educação permanente
items.rights_note: Revista Brasileira de Educação Médica 30(1), 2006. DOI 10.1590/S0100-55022006000100010. Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 (CC-BY-NC 4.0). SciELO Brazil. Portuguese-language Brazilian article on transitioning from the biomedical to the biopsychosocial model in medical education and hospital practice. Author Mario Alfredo De Marco is from São Paulo. Portuguese-language medical education context distinct from Engel's original Anglo-American psychiatric framing.
